Assign Related Colors to Subcategories

Source: R/assign_color_ranges.R
assign_color_ranges.Rd

Assign color ranges to subcategories nested within broader categories. Each parent category is associated with one or two colors, from which the required number of subtype colors is generated.

Usage

assign_color_ranges(
  item_list,
  color_palette,
  fallback_color = NULL,
  single_color = "middle"
)

Arguments

item_list

A named list. Each element contains the names of the subcategories belonging to one parent category.

color_palette

A named list of color specifications. Names should correspond to names in item_list. Each element should contain one or two colors accepted by create_color_range().

fallback_color

Optional, a single color used for items for which no corresponding color palette is provided. If NULL (default), items without a corresponding palette are omitted from the returned list.

single_color

Character string defining which color is returned when n = 1 and two endpoint colors are supplied. One of "middle" (default), returning the color between both endpoints; "first", returning the first endpoint; or "last", returning the second endpoint.

Value

A named list with one element per parent category. Each element is a named character vector mapping subcategory names to colors. Items without a corresponding palette may be omitted depending on fallback_color, and empty items are always omitted.

Details

For each parent category represented in color_palette, the number of required colors is determined from the corresponding element of item_list, and a color range is generated with create_color_range().

Empty items in item_list will be omitted.

If no fallback_color is specified items in item_list without a corresponding color specification will be omitted. I a valid color for fallback_color is specified, these items will get assigned this color.

Examples

item_set <- list(
  item1 = c("var1", "var2", "var3", "var4"),
  item2 = c("varA", "varB", "varC"))

palettes <- list(
  item1 = c("#FFF7BC", "#D95F0E"),
  item2 = c("#DEEBF7", "#08519C"))

assign_color_ranges(item_list = item_set, color_palette = palettes)
#> $item1
#>      var1      var2      var3      var4 
#> "#FFF7BC" "#F2C482" "#E69248" "#D95F0E" 
#> 
#> $item2
#>      varA      varB      varC 
#> "#DEEBF7" "#739ECA" "#08519C" 
#>
